evals.name: already-merged-terminal
evals.expected_output: PR is already merged. G7 short-circuits — the checklist reports all gates passing, Verdict: MERGED with the mergedAt timestamp, no actions taken, no sub-agents spawned.
assertions: Output shows the G1-G7 checklist
Verdict line reads 'Verdict: MERGED' and includes the mergedAt timestamp
No sub-agents are spawned and no mutating gh commands are run
Only the primary gh pr view call is made (plus at most the GraphQL thread fetch); no merge/edit/comment calls

evals.name: fresh-agent-pr-comments-and-ci
evals.prompt: Get this PR over the line: https://github.com/acme-corp/user-service/pull/89
evals.expected_output: Fresh agent-drafted PR. G1 ok, G2 mergeable, G3 fails (two unresolved review comments — one a clear naming fix, one a design question), G4 fails (lint red), G5 draft, G6 no approval. The skill resolves the clear comment (fix + reply + mark thread resolved), replies-and-@mentions the commenter on the design question leaving that thread open, fixes lint locally and pushes. It does NOT block waiting for remote CI — it reports CI re-running. Verdict: IN PROGRESS or BLOCKED with the open design comment surfaced.
assertions: The clear/mechanical comment is fixed, replied to, AND its thread is marked resolved via the resolveReviewThread GraphQL mutation
The design-decision comment is replied to with an @-mention of the commenter and its thread is left UNRESOLVED
Lint is reproduced/fixed locally and pushed; the skill does not busy-wait on remote CI
The verdict reflects that CI is re-running and unverified, not a false 'all green'
No --admin or --auto flag appears anywhere; no merge is attempted

evals.name: draft-not-flipped-while-ci-red
evals.expected_output: Draft PR with a genuinely failing, unfixed CI check (e.g. an out-of-scope/flaky failure the skill cannot fix). The skill does NOT flip the draft to ready while CI is failing-and-unfixed, escalates the out-of-scope failure in the terminal, and does not request review or merge.
assertions: gh pr ready is NOT run because CI is failing and unfixed
No reviewer is requested (G5 not satisfied) and no merge is attempted
The out-of-scope/unfixable CI failure is surfaced in the terminal as a human blocker, not silenced or worked around
No check or workflow is disabled/edited to bypass the failure

evals.name: all-green-approved-merges
evals.expected_output: G1-G6 all pass and mergeStateStatus is CLEAN. The skill runs the docs drift-check (best-effort, non-blocking) then merges inline with gh pr merge --squash (no --auto, no --admin). Reports the merge.
assertions: The merge runs inline (not via a sub-agent) using gh pr merge --squash
The merge command contains NO --auto and NO --admin flag
A docs drift-check is performed before merging but never blocks the merge
Merge is only attempted because all G1-G6 pass and mergeStateStatus == CLEAN

evals.name: behind-base-rebase-with-lease
evals.prompt: Can you get https://github.com/acme-corp/web-app/pull/156 merged? it says it's out of date
evals.expected_output: PR is BEHIND base, not yet reviewed. The skill rebases onto base and force-pushes WITH --force-with-lease (never a bare --force, never a merge-commit update), notes CI will re-run, and returns rather than waiting. Rebase is done early, before requesting review.
assertions: The branch is rebased onto base (git rebase), NOT updated via a merge commit / gh pr update-branch
The force-push uses --force-with-lease; a bare 'git push --force' never appears
The skill notes CI will re-run after the rebase and does not busy-wait on it
Rebase happens before review is requested (so a later rebase can't dismiss an approval)

evals.name: reviewer-selected-no-self-assign
evals.expected_output: Ready, green PR by a bot/agent author, no reviewer requested, no approval. The skill selects a reviewer by priority (user-named > CODEOWNERS > file git-history > recent contributors), excludes the author, requests 1-2 reviewers, and reports who+why. If the strongest human candidate is the operator running the skill, it surfaces 'ready for your review' in the terminal rather than self-assigning them.
assertions: Reviewer selection follows the priority order and uses file git-history (or CODEOWNERS) rather than picking an arbitrary name
The PR author is excluded from candidates and at most 1-2 reviewers are requested
The skill reports WHO was selected and WHY
If the best candidate is the operator, it surfaces 'ready for your review' in the terminal instead of self-assigning

evals.name: waiting-on-review-returns
evals.expected_output: G1-G5 pass, a reviewer is already requested but no approval yet (G6 fails), G7 fails. There is nothing mechanical left to do — it's an indeterminate human wait. The skill takes no action, leaves no nagging comment, and returns a clear BLOCKED-needs-human verdict naming the awaited reviewer.
assertions: No mutating gh command is run (no merge, no re-request, no comment)
No --auto and no --admin anywhere; no merge attempted
No nagging comment or @-mention is left on the PR to chase the reviewer
Verdict is BLOCKED — needs human, identifying that it's waiting on the requested reviewer's approval

evals.name: intentional-wip-killswitch
evals.expected_output: PR has a 'wip' label AND the most recent author comment says 'still working on the retry logic, don't merge yet'. The signal is live, not stale. The skill recognizes the kill-switch: it does NOT strip the label, does NOT proceed to other gates, and reports in the terminal that the author is intentionally holding the PR.
assertions: The wip label is NOT removed and the title is not edited
The skill does not proceed to fix CI / resolve comments / request review once it judges the hold intentional
It surfaces in the terminal that the WIP signal looks intentional and asks the operator to confirm
No merge is attempted
